## Upstream changes 2.37.2 -> 2.38.0

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the notes contain bugfixes, security-relevant permission fixes, and translation updates, with no breaking changes and no new companion-service requirement.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no renamed, removed or newly required variables. `ROUTER_BASE_PATH` normalization was already shipped in 2.37.2 (the baseline), not this range, and the compose file doesn't set that variable anyway.

### Data and dependencies
- none. No database version requirement, no migration, no changed ports or paths called out in the 2.38.0 notes.
- Worth noting as access-control fixes, not deployment changes: "Non-admin users able to access another user's playback session", "Media progress endpoints not checking library item access", "Library list including every library when access to all libraries is off and the allow list is empty", "Empty tag allow list treated as access to every book, podcast, and series" — these are security fixes to apply, not configuration the host must change.
- The image's internal Node.js version moved 24.22.1 -> 24.22.3 per the registry diff; this is inside the image and not reflected in the release notes text, but it's not a dependency the compose file pins or needs to track.

### Before applying
- None required beyond the normal pull/recreate. No manual migration command or config edit is indicated by the notes.
- Good practice given the access-control fixes: after upgrading, review library/tag allow-list settings for any users where "access to all libraries" is off, since the previous behaviour silently over-granted access.

### Notes read
- v2.38.0 (2026-11-17), the target release.
- v2.37.2 (2026-10-23), the baseline currently running, read only to confirm nothing in it is miscounted as new in this range.

## Upstream changes 1.19.0 -> 1.20.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no companion-service version mismatch, but this upgrade changes how Docker env files are loaded, adds new Celery queues and a reverse-proxy route the template must supply, requires `docker compose up -d` (not a plain restart), and ships six new Alembic migrations.

### Breaking changes
- `docker/envs/core-services/shared.env` is **no longer loaded**: *"`docker/envs/core-services/shared.env` is **no longer loaded**. Move common API, worker, and Beat settings to `api-worker.env` before recreating containers."* This template's compose file does not use `shared.env`/`api-worker.env` at all (it sets shared values via the `x-app-env` anchor and `.env`), so this specific migration step does not apply here — but any operator who hand-edited a `shared.env` copy for this stack must move those settings into `.env`/the compose anchor instead.
- New Celery queues `human_input_delivery` and `human_input_contact_sync` are required: *"Custom `CELERY_QUEUES`, `CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES`, or Celery `--queues` lists must provide an active consumer for each queue alongside existing subscriptions."* The template's `worker` service does not set `CELERY_QUEUES`/`CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES` explicitly (it relies on image defaults), so this is likely already covered — confirm the image's default queue list includes both before relying on it.
- New reverse-proxy route required for HITL IM webhooks: *"In `WEBHOOK` mode, forward `/callbacks/human-input/v2/im/` to the API service... The bundled nginx template already includes this rule; add its equivalent to custom nginx, Ingress, or other reverse proxy configurations."* This template vendors Dify's own nginx config (not a custom reimplementation), so it should already carry this rule — but CI's drift check against upstream nginx config must be confirmed green for 1.20.0 before trusting it blindly.
- `docker compose up -d` is required to pick up environment file changes: *"Apply changes with `docker compose up -d`; a plain restart does not reload environment files."*
- Plain Docker image behavior change, not app code: `OPENAPI_ENABLED` now defaults to `true` (was `false`), exposing `/openapi/v1/*` endpoints by default.

### Variables
- `OPENAPI_ENABLED`: default flips `true` (was `false`) — exposes OpenAPI endpoints unless explicitly set to `false`. Not currently in `.env.example`; add explicitly if this should stay closed.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_HITL_IM`: default flips `true` (was `false`) — enables New HITL IM/Contacts/approval UI by default. Not currently in `.env.example`.
- `HUMAN_INPUT_GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `HUMAN_INPUT_IM_EVENT_TRANSPORT_MODE`, `FILE_SCAN_ENABLED` (and related `FILE_SCAN_*` vars), `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_AGENT_V2_IN_CHATFLOW`, `DEEPEVAL_DISABLE_DOTENV`/`DEEPEVAL_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT` — all new, all default off/safe except as noted above. None currently appear in `.env.example`; they'll fall back to image defaults unless added.
- `DIFY_AGENT_OPENSHELL_SHARED_MOUNT_PATH`: removed upstream ("Shared-volume Home Snapshots are no longer supported by the OpenShell backend"). Not present in this template's `.env.example` or compose file — no action needed.
- `DIFY_AGENT_OPENSHELL_DRIVER_CONFIG`: now optional upstream. Not present in this template — no action needed (this template runs `DIFY_AGENT_RUNTIME_BACKEND=local`, not OpenShell).
- `EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_VINEXT`: removed from Web Docker image builds. The template's `.env.example` still sets `EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_VINEXT=false` — this line is now a no-op and can be deleted, but leaving it does no harm since Compose simply ignores an env var the image no longer reads.
- `TRIGGER_URL`: notes say *"Set to the public HTTPS API origin for IM callbacks... Update the IM provider configuration when this origin changes."* The template already derives `TRIGGER_URL: https://${DIFY_HOSTNAME}` in the compose `x-app-env` block — this is an existing template behavior, not a new requirement from this release.
- New `envs/core-services/urls.defaults` / `urls.env` consolidation for public URLs — this template already derives all nine public URLs from `DIFY_HOSTNAME` directly in compose (`x-app-env`), bypassing the urls.env mechanism entirely. No action needed; the template's approach supersedes this upstream file reorganization.

### Data and dependencies
- Six new Alembic migrations, head moves from `53c10126d551` to `f8b6e2c4a901`: adds `human_input_im_sync_runs` column, personal access token tables, file scanner tables, Evaluation tables (apply to CE too, even though unused), and a migration-branch merge. Notes state: *"none of the six revisions require a separate manual backfill command."* `MIGRATION_ENABLED=true` (already the template default) handles this automatically via `api`/`worker`/`worker_beat`.
- Plugin daemon bump to `0.6.15-local` is already reflected in this repo's compose file (`plugin-daemon: ...0.6.15-local@sha256:14aebd...`) and `.env.example` default — correctly pre-applied, not an outstanding action.
- OpenShell-specific requirements (gateway 0.1.3+, `DIFY_AGENT_OPENSHELL_SHELLCTL_AUTH_TOKEN` rotation, runtime image rebuild) do not apply: this template runs `DIFY_AGENT_RUNTIME_BACKEND=local` with the local sandbox, not OpenShell.
- No companion-service version requirement (Postgres/Redis/Weaviate) is named in these notes, so the verdict is not forced to DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED on that ground.

### Before applying
- Back up the database, Weaviate volume, app storage, plugin daemon volume, and `.env` before upgrading, per upstream: *"Back up your database, vector-store data, uploaded files, plugin daemon storage, Agent workspace storage, deployment secrets, and environment files."*
- Bump the four coupled image pins together in the compose `x-images` block: `DIFY_API_IMAGE_VERSION`, `DIFY_WEB_IMAGE_VERSION`, `DIFY_LOCAL_SANDBOX_IMAGE_VERSION`, `DIFY_AGENT_BACKEND_IMAGE_VERSION`, all to `1.20.0`, keeping plugin daemon at `0.6.15-local` (already pinned there).
- Decide and set `OPENAPI_ENABLED=false` in `.env` explicitly if you do not want `/openapi/v1/*` reachable by default.
- Decide and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_HITL_IM=false` in `.env` explicitly if you do not want the new HITL approval UI active by default; otherwise plan for the `TRIGGER_URL`-based IM webhook callback route (already present via vendored nginx config) and confirm the worker consumes the two new Celery queues.
- Confirm (via CI's nginx drift check or manual diff) that the vendored `nginx/conf.d/default.conf.template` for 1.20.0 includes the new `/callbacks/human-input/v2/im/` route before enabling HITL IM.
- Use `docker compose stop -t -1`, pull, then `docker compose up -d` (not a bare restart) so migrations run and env files reload, per the standard sequence in the notes.
- Keep `SECRET_KEY`, `PASSWORD_PEPPER` (if set), and the Local sandbox auth token unchanged across the upgrade, per upstream guidance.

### Notes read
- `langgenius/dify` release notes for `1.20.0` (full body) and `1.19.0` (baseline, read for context only — no action items taken from it beyond confirming what was already true at the current version).
